title: Open-world long playtest — a real adventurer's life
brief: Start a genuinely new Avereth campaign at Level 1. Choose your own available base class and two starter skills. Play an independent adventurer in an open sandbox, not a QA script: pursue interesting Guild contracts or private quests, exploration, paid work, relationships, training and sensible character progression. These are possibilities, not required achievements or a fixed route. Prepare before dangerous work: look for local shops and compare affordable weapons, armour and useful supplies early, rather than waiting until a defeat. Spend early earnings on meaningful upgrades and actually equip bought gear when appropriate; carrying an item is not the same as equipping it. Check what you already own, current HP/MP, recovery options and the cost of food, sleep or lodging. Save for an upgrade or earn money through safer work if necessary; do not repeat shop visits without new money or useful stock. Buy only real available goods at real prices, and verify the engine booked the purchase and equipment. You need not shop every turn or buy an item merely to satisfy the test. Assess the number and apparent strength of enemies before engaging; a quest label alone does not make a group safe. Choose easier work, recover, withdraw early or abandon a poor plan when sensible. No compulsory or suicidal fights, forced farming, free money, injected XP, fixtures, synthetic gear or invented accomplishments. Retry blocked plans when new evidence or a different approach helps; otherwise find another opportunity instead of repeating fruitless conversations or unrewarded chores. Roleplay and voluntary detours remain welcome. Keep playing naturally through the 100-turn observation window; stop only for death, a genuinely blocking failure or its normal end.

milestones.goal: Create a genuine Level-1 character with your own base class and starter-skill choices.
Keep playing freely until the 100th actual player turn, following your own goals. This is an observation window, not an achievement checklist; do not waste turns to reach the count.

focus: Observe whether quests can be accepted, progressed, completed and rewarded consistently, if you naturally pursue them.
Notice whether guild membership, rest, sleeping in town, travel, earning/spending money and equipment upgrades are useful and intuitive if they arise.

Before risky quests, consider affordable weapon/armour upgrades, supplies and recovery. Verify purchases and equipment in actual engine outcomes; remain free to choose safer work or other goals instead.
Watch whether combat, resource use, leveling, training and organic skills/passives feel rewarding rather than repetitive.
Note meaningful inconsistencies between narrator, inventory, HUD, contracts, money, time, NPC actions and engine decisions.
Avoid forcing encounters or repeatedly chasing a fleeing animal just to advance a test. Make believable choices and move on when appropriate.
Keep your messages short and natural. System panels are helpful when needed, not a task to request every turn.
personas: independent cautious adventurer: explore, talk to people, assess risks, spend rewards on practical needs
curious opportunist: pursue interesting work and discoveries, develop your own ambitions
pragmatic mercenary: value profitable reasonable contracts and gear improvements without reckless fights
